prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm operations and maintenance system supports safe, reliable electrical generation, personnel safety, asset integrity, availability, and environmental protection. Boundary includes offshore generation assets, supporting marine/shore facilities, operational personnel, participating external organizations, and enabling cybersecurity, communications, fire protection, and backup power. Physical boundary starts at turbine structures; electrical/export boundary ends at Grid Interface Relay. Public grid assets beyond the agreed connection and unrelated port operations are excluded.
Canonical names identify parts, actors, states, and controlled items. Aliases: Glassfin = Turbine Controller; Morrowick = Offshore Substation; Pale Lantern = Weather Service.
Turbine Controller controls an individual turbine. Turbine subsystems/equipment include Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, and Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone assesses turbine blades. Offshore Substation provides electrical collection/switching; Main Transformer is a substation asset; Export Cable Monitor is an export-system asset. SCADA Gateway provides supervisory monitoring/control interface.
Shore Control Room accommodates authorized operators and performs continuous monitoring/dispatch coordination. Fleet Dispatch Console coordinates resources; Maintenance Planning Engine prepares/sequences maintenance. Marine coordination covers Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel, Helideck, and applicable vessel procedures. North Access Scanner, South Access Scanner, and Personnel Tracking Console support workforce access management. Warehouse System and Spares Hub coordinate inventory/replenishment. Weather Service supplies external weather information; Metocean Buoy supplies offshore environmental observations. External interfaces include grid dispatch, port support, suppliers, and emergency response organizations; other specific item exchanges remain undefined.
Lifecycle: commissioning/acceptance, routine operation, major refurbishment, decommissioning. Commissioning requires documented handover/verification. Normal-service decisions require validated asset status, approved procedures, current forecasts, and applicable grid instructions. Maintenance considers condition, resources, access, production, and prioritized fault severity. Safety requires authorized work, controlled hazards, personnel/vessel accountability. Environmental objectives require pollution prevention, minimized marine disturbance, prompt incident response. End-of-life supports safe isolation, removal planning, residual-record transfer to responsible organization.

New part:
S045: Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft, and Service Operations Vessel represent marine resources that may support offshore work.
S046: Helideck is included as an access facility for activities supported by helicopter operations.
S047: Personnel Tracking Console represents the personnel location and accountability function.
S048: Warehouse System and Spares Hub represent the inventory and logistics context for maintenance materials.
S049: Work Permit Portal and Cybersecurity Gateway represent enabling functions that support controlled and secure operations.
S050: The operating concept also recognizes grid, emergency response, communications, and port support as external or enabling capabilities.
S051: The system architecture separates offshore equipment, operational services, and shore-based decision functions while preserving defined interfaces between them.
S052: The SCADA Gateway provides a controlled boundary for supervisory data exchange between offshore assets and shore-based operations.
S053: For this concept, SCADA Gateway is designated Juniper Vale as its operational alias.
S054: The Maintenance Planning Engine supports work preparation by organizing maintenance needs, resource considerations, and planning constraints.
S055: For this concept, Maintenance Planning Engine is designated Thistle Crown as its operational alias.
S056: The Shore Control Room is the principal shore-based setting for monitoring and coordinating wind farm operations.
S057: For this concept, Shore Control Room is designated Amber Quay as its operational alias.
S058: These three components have distinct responsibilities and are treated as cooperating parts of one operational system.
S059: The SCADA Gateway mediates supervisory exchanges and supports consistent access to operational information.
S060: The Turbine Controller performs local turbine control functions within the offshore equipment environment.
S061: The Turbine Controller produces the Pitch Deviation Notice for operational handling.
S062: The SCADA Engineer maintains the configuration and technical integrity of supervisory interfaces.
S063: The Control Engineer uses the shore-based operational picture to assess equipment status and coordinate response.
S064: The Shore Control Room provides a shared operational context for personnel responsible for offshore assets.
S065: The Duty Planner uses the Maintenance Planning Engine to prepare and review maintenance activities.
S066: The Maintenance Planning Engine supports planning decisions without replacing the judgment of the Duty Planner.
S067: The Weather Service contributes environmental information to operational planning and coordination.
S068: The Marine Coordinator considers offshore conditions and vessel availability when coordinating access to work sites.
S069: The Fleet Dispatch Console provides a fleet-level view of dispatch activity for operational coordination.
S070: The Work Permit Portal supports authorization processes that govern work under controlled conditions.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
